To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we find a semiclassical description of SU(2) lattice gauge theory, that the expectation value of any polynomial in the canonical operators can be computed in a straightforward manner, and that the expectation values are sharply peaked around the classical phase space point, i.e. the quantum fluctuations are small.
The expectation value of the gauge potential is given by the gauge potential evaluated at the phase space point.

the expectation values for a general SU(2) coherent state are given by the classical values of the operators in the limit of infinite lattice volume, and that the first order quantum correction is given by a sum of terms of the form $1/2\, \mathrm{Tr}\left( [A_i, A_j]^2\right)$ where $A_i$ are the classical gauge fields.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics:
  1. The construction of coherent states for general quantum gauge field theories.
  2. A detailed study of the quantum fluctuations of the gauge field around the classical solution.
the following topics: (i) We investigate the expectation value of a general polynomial of the canonical operators in terms of a classical phase space point.
the following topics: 1. We will study the semiclassical properties of the SU(2) coherent state.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantum fluctuations are small and of a Gaussian nature, but the precise size and nature of the quantum corrections depend on the observable in question.

the expectation value of a general polynomial of canonical variables is a polynomial of the same variables, but with the classical variables replaced by their expectation values, plus a quantum correction term.
the expectation value of the Wilson loop is a smooth function of the classical loop, while the expectation value of a general polynomial is a smooth function only of the classical phase space point.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now calculate the quantum expectation values of any observable in any semiclassical gauge theory.
we are able to compute expectation values of general polynomials for a given semiclassical state.
the quantum fluctuations of the expectation values are of order 2/3 of the classical fluctuations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum fluctuations in the gauge sector of the theory are suppressed by a factor of 1/g^2.

, for the SU(2) gauge group and in the large N limit, the expectation value of the Wilson loop is given by its classical value plus quantum corrections which are proportional to the area of the loop and the curvature of the loop, respectively, and which vanish in the limit of a large loop.
, while the expectation value of the gauge field is peaked at a point in the gauge orbit space, the expectation value of its covariant derivative is peaked at a different point.
